title.narrative: INDOTH1.3 Trans Fund subgrants increase THRDs resources to address trans priorities such as (nonexhaustive list) lack of legal gender recognition, depathologization, violence, poverty, education, employment, humanitarian aid and transinclusive health care

description.narrative: INDOTH1.3 Trans Fund subgrants increase THRDs resources to address trans priorities such as (nonexhaustive list) lack of legal gender recognition, depathologization, violence, poverty, education, employment, humanitarian aid and transinclusive health care

comment.narrative: BASOTH1.3 Trans Fund baseline to be set participatory with future THRDs and their organisations that will be financially supported by this action during Inception Phase months 13
TAROTH1.3 Trans Fund THRDs supported by this action through a Trans Fund subgrant make progress toward addressing trans priorities 25 increase in selfreported progress

CUROTH1.3 Trans Fund supported THRDs and their organization to increase resources addressing following issues a Making autonomous decisionsTrans organisations and groups empowered by general support have gained the autonomy to make decisions that benefit both themselves and the communities they serve. For instance with support from ITF Transgender Japan successfully incorporated as an autonomous organisation in Japan in December 2023.b Setting their own social change agendas and responding to evolving conditionsTrans groups and organisations can now adapt to changing circumstances in their regions and contexts. For example Trans Dynamics Morocco developed a comprehensive glossary of trans terms in accessible language addressing diverse gender identities. This glossary created collaboratively with trans individuals is the first thorough reference document of its kind in Morocco contributing to trans feminist activism.c Caring for themselves and their communitiesTrans groups have prioritised mental health and community care supported by grants like those from ITF. For instance Trans Dynamics Morocco provided free weekly therapy sessions for staff and community members benefiting 20 trans activists in 2023.d Building power and influencing wider movementsTrans Dynamics is an active member of the Civil Council for the Fight Against All Forms of Discrimination collaborating with over 14 feminist and communitybased organisations. Their joint advocacy efforts including contributions to annual reports on systemic discrimination and work with allies like Generations G amplify trans voices and advocate for decriminalisation amidst ongoing national conversations on penal code reform in Morocco. 2023

description.narrative: INDOTH1.4 CrossCutting Issues number of Intersex Fund and Trans Fund subgrants that mainstream this actions crosscutting issues of a) gender equality; b) children and youth, c) HIV/AIDS; d) labour rights and core labour standards

comment.narrative: BASOTH1.4 CrossCutting Issues 0 IHRDs andor THRDs and their organizations located in Africa Asia andor the Pacific receive Intersex Fund and Trans Fund subgrants through this action that mainstream crosscutting issues
TAROTH1.4 CrossCutting Issues 100 of Intersex Fund and Trans Fund subgrants under this action mainstream crosscutting issues

CUROTH1.4. 3 IHRDled groups and 6 THRDled groups 100 of subgrants under this action 2022 Trans Fund in particular took further crosscutting issues in their support to THRDs and their organization as following a Gender equality Trans Dynamics Morocco has actively engaged with the broader feminist and womens movement in Morocco aligning its work with gender equality principles. This strategic alignment necessitates prioritising gender equality in all organisational endeavours and project activities.b Children and youth Both Trans Dynamics Morocco and Transgender Japan have adopted a youthcentred approach in their organisational development and project implementation efforts. Additionally trans youth are meaningfully represented at leadership levels within both organisations.c HIVAIDS Both Trans Dynamics Morocco and Transgender Japan integrate HIVAIDS issues into their programming and strategies for accessing affirming healthcare.d Labour rights and core labour standards In 2023 Trans Dynamics Morocco prioritised mental health and staff wellness initiatives aiming to create a safe space for staff communication and resiliencebuilding. This focus on mental health contributes to improved team dynamics within the organisation.2023

CUROTH2.1 The Intersex Fund conducted a total of six oneonone accompaniment and technical assistance interventions to BoM subgrantee partners and the Trans Fund conducted a total of 12 oneonone accompaniment and technical assistance interventions to BoM subgrantee partners. 2022 Intersex Asia held an inperson capacitybuilding training with 22 IHRDs. 2022 The demand for technical support has led SIPD to organise 18 online engagements with intersex human rights defenders IHRDs throughout the year focusing on strengthening their capabilities in promoting and protecting the intersex community. In addition the ITFs 2023 capacitybuilding program benefited 43 individuals through webinars on strategic financing and organisational effectiveness resulting in improved financial management policy policy implementation and organisational development among partner organisations. 2023

title.narrative: INDOTH2.2 Workshops Enhanced organisational capacities in the area of promotion and protection of human rights, with emphasis on advocacy for trans and intersex rights, for THRDs, IHRDs and duty bearers in Africa, Asia and the Pacific

description.narrative: INDOTH2.2 Workshops Enhanced organisational capacities in the area of promotion and protection of human rights, with emphasis on advocacy for trans and intersex rights, for THRDs, IHRDs and duty bearers in Africa, Asia and the Pacific

comment.narrative: BASOTH2.2 Workshops existing competences in the area of promotion and protection of the human rights of trans and intersex persons among IHRDs THRDs and duty bearers
TAROTH2.2 Workshops 25 increase in level of competences in the area of promotion and protection of the human rights of trans and intersex persons among IHRDs THRDs and duty bearers

CUROTH2.2 The Trans Fund provided three partners with technical advice on safety and security. 2022 SIPD held 3 workshops on health gender and equity from government agencies civil society and the intersex community. IHRDs gained increased knowledge about and comprehension of the challenges that the intersex community faces and their desired strategies to protect their rights in society. 2022 SIPD embarked on capacity strengthening initiatives by providing handson visits and tailored skills training to intersexled groups in Kenya and Tanzania addressing programmatic administrative and strategic communication needs. Through two capacitybuilding trainings conducted with Tanzania Voice of Humanity and Intersex Persons Society of Kenya IPSK SIPD established a peer network of intersex organisation leaders to advance intersex rights in Africa. Followup meetings and ongoing support further enhanced the organisational capacities of six intersexled organisations facilitating their incorporation and registration processes. Similarly the International Trans Fund ITF provided comprehensive support to grantee partners including capacity building in advocacy organisational effectiveness resource mobilisation and financial management. 2023

IHRDs gained increased knowledge about and comprehension of the challenges that the intersex community faces and their desired strategies to protect their rights in society. 2022 SIPD embarked on capacity strengthening initiatives by providing handson visits and tailored skills training to intersexled groups in Kenya and Tanzania addressing programmatic administrative and strategic communication needs. Through two capacitybuilding trainings conducted with Tanzania Voice of Humanity and Intersex Persons Society of Kenya IPSK SIPD established a peer network of intersex organisation leaders to advance intersex rights in Africa. Followup meetings and ongoing support further enhanced the organisational capacities of six intersexled organisations facilitating their incorporation and registration processes. Similarly the International Trans Fund ITF provided comprehensive support to grantee partners including capacity building in advocacy organisational effectiveness resource mobilisation and financial management. 2023

title.narrative: INDOTH3.2 Asia & Pacific/Trans Asia Pacific Trans Network strengthened in terms of membership (width, depth, diversity), information, networking, exchange of best practices

description.narrative: INDOTH3.2 Asia & Pacific/Trans Asia Pacific Trans Network strengthened in terms of membership (width, depth, diversity), information, networking, exchange of best practices

comment.narrative: BASOTH3.2 Asia PacificTrans APTN works with a small base of THRDs and THRDled groups does not convene at the regional level and has limited possibilities to exchange experience
TAROTH3.2 Asia PacificTrans APTN has expanded and diversified convenes gathers up to 50 THRDs from 15 THRD groups and exchange best practices for regional advocacy

CUROTH3.2. APTN deepened its knowledge exchange around conversation therapy and hate crimes 2021 APTN strengthened networks through the sub regional convenings in 202223 and the THRD capacity building workshop in collaboration with ITF and regional consultations to be convened by APTN in 2023 2022 In the period spanning 2022 to 2023 APTN organised two subregional convening meetings for trans activists and transled groups and organisations. The South East Asia Convening took place in Bangkok while the South Asia Convening was held in Nepal with a total participation of 96 trans activists. Topics covered included access to genderaffirming health services combating violence such as transphobic hate crimes and conversion therapy addressing mental health and wellbeing and advancing legal rights and protections for trans people. Additionally APTN forged partnerships with allies and Civil Society Organizations CSOs including healthcare providers feminist organisations National Human Rights Commissions and government representatives through collaborative sessions and networking events. In 2023 APTN in collaboration with SEED Malaysia organised a roundtable discussion in Malaysia building upon its Conversion Therapy Initiatives. The event convened over 20 stakeholders including trans activists CSOs psychiatrists health professionals legal practitioners and the National Human Rights Institution NHRI. The primary focus was to address the pressing issue of conversion therapy practices endorsed by the Malaysian government. APTN presented regional research findings and shared success stories of banning conversion therapy from various Asian countries facilitating knowledge exchange on conversion therapy and hate crimes. Furthermore APTN enhanced its networks through subregional convenings in 202223 and a THRD capacitybuilding workshop conducted in collaboration with the ITF along with regional consultations planned for 2023. 2023

title.narrative: INDOTH3.3 Africa/Intersex informal African IHRD network African Intersex Movement (AIM) formalized and strengthened through technical support, internships and convening

description.narrative: INDOTH3.3 Africa/Intersex informal African IHRD network African Intersex Movement (AIM) formalized and strengthened through technical support, internships and convening

comment.narrative: BASOTH3.3 AfricaIntersex there is a nascent African IHRDs network that is tentatively called the African Intersex Movement AIM AIM and its members have limited opportunities to receive technical support to exchange staff and to convene

TAROTH3.3 AfricaIntersex There is a formal African intersex network that is providing support to individual African IHRDs and their organisations up to 22 IHRDs and 10 IHRDled groups in Africa receive technical support second up to 9 interns to SIPD and convene

CUROTH3.3 AIM has institutionalised including receiving first funding developing a strategic plan and creating a secretariat. AIM made new connections with IHRDs in Nigeria Ghana the Democratic Republic of Congo Cameroon and Tanzania. 2021 SIPD continues to provide technical support to AIM and we played a significant role in its expansion. SIPD has made over five referrals of new IHRDs to AIM especially from East Africa. With SIPDs technical support AIM has strengthened and also expanded its linkages with regional funders and other networks such as PAI UHAI and Iranti. SIPD supported AIM with their resource mobilization and the network was able to secure its very first funding in 2022. 2022 Throughout 2023 SIPD played a crucial role in providing technical support to the African Intersex Movement AIM. Notably SIPDs assistance was instrumental during the preparation and execution of the 3rd African Intersex Movement Conference held in Kenya in February. The conference served as a significant platform for AIM convening intersex human rights defenders IHRDs from across Africa to exchange experiences and devise collective advocacy strategies tailored to the continents specific challenges. With a participation of 40 individuals from 10 African countries including the appointment of Kenyas first openly intersex Commissioner the conference marked a milestone in African intersex activism. Subsequently SIPD continued to offer technical assistance to the newly formed and expanded AIM committee. This support encompassed various online and inperson engagements aimed at enhancing strategic planning particularly in response to the recent African Commission on Human and Peoples Rights Resolution 552. Discussions revolved around comprehending the African human rights systems structure and the implications of Resolution 552 for advocacy nationallevel domestication movement building and resource mobilisation. As a result of SIPDs support AIM made significant strides in institutionalising its operations securing its first funding developing a strategic plan and establishing a secretariat. Furthermore SIPD facilitated AIMs expansion and strengthened its connections with intersex human rights defenders in Nigeria Ghana the Democratic Republic of Congo Cameroon and Tanzania. 2023

The conference served as a significant platform for AIM convening intersex human rights defenders IHRDs from across Africa to exchange experiences and devise collective advocacy strategies tailored to the continents specific challenges. With a participation of 40 individuals from 10 African countries including the appointment of Kenyas first openly intersex Commissioner the conference marked a milestone in African intersex activism. Subsequently SIPD continued to offer technical assistance to the newly formed and expanded AIM committee. This support encompassed various online and inperson engagements aimed at enhancing strategic planning particularly in response to the recent African Commission on Human and Peoples Rights Resolution 552. Discussions revolved around comprehending the African human rights systems structure and the implications of Resolution 552 for advocacy nationallevel domestication movement building and resource mobilisation. As a result of SIPDs support AIM made significant strides in institutionalising its operations securing its first funding developing a strategic plan and establishing a secretariat. Furthermore SIPD facilitated AIMs expansion and strengthened its connections with intersex human rights defenders in Nigeria Ghana the Democratic Republic of Congo Cameroon and Tanzania. 2023

CUROTH3.4. title.narrative: INDOTH3.5 Regional Networking/ CrossCutting Issues All regional networking integrates this actions crosscutting issues of a) gender equality; b) children and youth, c) HIV/AIDS; d) labour rights and core labour standards

description.narrative: INDOTH3.5 Regional Networking/ CrossCutting Issues All regional networking integrates this actions crosscutting issues of a) gender equality; b) children and youth, c) HIV/AIDS; d) labour rights and core labour standards

comment.narrative: BASOTH3.5 Regional Networking CrossCutting Issues All regional networks engage with crosscutting issues but not always with clear intention to outcomes.
TAROTH3.5 Regional Networking CrossCutting Issues 100 of regional networking activities integrate this actions crosscutting issues

CUROTH3.5 AIM and Intersex Asia programming centred the rights of intersex children and youth gender equality and labour rights. APTNs work on conversion therapy centred children and youth. Programming of AIN members centred HIVAIDS and gender equality. 2021 APTNs convenings had a significant focus on the accessibility of transaffirming care. The accessibility delved deeply into the challenges surrounding HIVAIDS exposure among trans communities and the availability of relevant healthcare services. Additionally Intersex Asia programming has been dedicated to advocating for the rights of intersex children and youth promoting gender equality and advancing labour rights. Similarly the work undertaken by APTN has been centred on combating conversion therapy with a specific focus on protecting children and youth. Finally the programming efforts of members within the Asia Pacific Intersex Network AIN have concentrated on addressing issues related to HIVAIDS and advancing gender equality. 2023

title.narrative: INDOTH4.1 Enhanced Trans and Intersex Advocacy visvis selected UN human rights mechanisms through shadow reporting, participation of IHRDs and THRDs in Universal Periodic Review (UPR), CEDAW and other Treaty Bodies (TB)/Special Procedures (SP), Side Events and Trans and Intersex Advocacy Weeks

description.narrative: INDOTH4.1 Enhanced Trans and Intersex Advocacy visvis selected UN human rights mechanisms through shadow reporting, participation of IHRDs and THRDs in Universal Periodic Review (UPR), CEDAW and other Treaty Bodies (TB)/Special Procedures (SP), Side Events and Trans and Intersex Advocacy Weeks

comment.narrative: BASOTH4.1 Trans and Intersex Advocacy There is limited THRD and IHRD engagement at the UN through shadow reporting participation of IHRDs and THRDs in Universal Periodic Review UPR CEDAW and other Treaty Bodies TBSpecial Procedures SP Side Events and Trans and Intersex Advocacy Weeks

TAROTH4.1 Increased Trans and Intersex Advocacy visvis selected international human rights mechanisms through shadow reporting participation of IHRDs and THRDs in Universal Periodic Review UPR CEDAW and other Treaty BodiesTBSpecial Procedures SP Side Events and Trans and Intersex Advocacy Weeks

CUROTH4.1 Successful intersex advocacy week virtual. Historic crossregional statement by 53 UN member states calling for concrete measures to combat harmful practices violence and discrimination against intersex persons. Civil society statement read at the HRCs 48th session calling for urgent action to address human rights violations against intersex persons. The statement was supported by 87 intersexled civil society organisations including SIPD 2021 Successful Trans Advocacy Week 2 annual Side Events regular high level meetings with UN officials 2021 ILGA developed a comprehensive program to engage with various stakeholders on the issue of intersex rights during the Intersex Advocacy at the 51st session of the Human Rights Council HRC51 in 2022.This included interacting with representatives from the Committee Against Torture CAT and the Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination Against Women CEDAW as well as the Special Rapporteur on the right to health and staff from the Office of the High Comissioner for Human Rights OHCHR. ILGA also held meetings with the staff of the permanent missions of Finland Australia Uruguay and Mexico. 2022 SIPD Uganda is part of the Intersex Policy Advisory Group and has contributed to the content in statements delivered at the Intersex Human Rights Side Event at the HRC51 2022 to elaborate on the most important elements of intersex rights and what we need for effective advocacy. Also SIPD Uganda continued its active involvement participating in the Intersex Policy Advisory Group and contributing to statements delivered at the Intersex Human Rights Side Event during HRC51. 2022 Moving to 2023 Intersex Advocacy Week concluded virtually with another significant milestone a historic crossregional statement by 53 UN member states calling for concrete measures to combat harmful practices. A civil society statement at HRCs 48th session also garnered widespread support from 87 intersexled civil society organisations including SIPD. APTN continued its contributions making a written submission for IE SOGIs call for inputs on health standards. Notably these efforts involved various activities such as engaging 12 Trans Human Rights Defenders at the HRC hosting 25 TAW Delegates organising training for 15 TAW Delegates delivering 3 Side Events at CSW issuing 4 Statements at HRC supporting 7 HRDs through Intersex Rights events engaging with over 20 Permanent Missions collaborating with 25 Intersexled Organisations receiving support from 98 LGBTI and Human Rights Groups organising 3 Side Events for TAW at HRC hosting about 75 individuals at JUNTES in So Paulo from over 35 countries conducting 2 Events at JUNTES releasing an Intersex Mapping Report on December 12 2023 and holding ILGA Worlds Closeddoor Round Table on Gender Identity and Trans Rights under CEDAW on October 12 2023. 2023

title.narrative: INDOTH4.2 African Commission Enhanced IHRD advocacy at the African Commission on Human and Peoples Rights (ACHPR) through participation IHRDs in NGO Forum, Resolution codrafting processes and Side Events

description.narrative: INDOTH4.2 African Commission Enhanced IHRD advocacy at the African Commission on Human and Peoples Rights (ACHPR) through participation IHRDs in NGO Forum, Resolution codrafting processes and Side Events

comment.narrative: BASOTH4.2 African Commission There is very nascent IHRD engagement at the ACHPR in the NGO Forum Resolution codrafting processes and Side Events
TAROTH4.2 African Commission Increased IHRD engagement at ACHPR involving up to 12 IHRDs in the NGO Forum Resolution codrafting processes and Side Events

CUROTH4.2. SIPD Uganda and The Centre for Human Rights convened a side event to launch a report on the human rights situation of intersex persons in Africa at the 73rd ordinary session of the African Commission on Human and Peoples rights in Banjul the Gambia. This event was held with the support of SIPD Ugandas partners The Intersex community of Zimbabwe ICoZ and the Intersex Persons Society of Kenya IPSK. 2022 SIPD played a pivotal role in facilitating activist participation at the 77th ordinary session of the ACHPR in Arusha. At this session Intersex Human Rights Defenders IHRDs engaged with commissioners participated in the NGO Forum and contributed to an intersex side event. This platform proved crucial in initiating discussions to enhance the Resolution and explore strategies for its implementation across African nations. Additionally SIPD received an invitation to meet with the EU delegation in Kampala where discussions focused on sharing best practices and showcasing activities from the BoM project. SIPD reaffirmed its commitment to supporting the intersex community especially in response to Ugandas enactment of the new AntiHomosexuality Act in 2023. Further strengthening their advocacy efforts SIPD Uganda and The Centre for Human Rights convened a side event during the 73rd ordinary session of the African Commission on Human and Peoples Rights in Banjul the Gambia. This event supported by SIPD Ugandas partners The Intersex community of Zimbabwe ICoZ and the Intersex Persons Society of Kenya IPSK served as the platform for launching a report on the human rights situation of intersex persons in Africa. Through collaborative initiatives like these organisations continue to raise awareness advocate for rights and advance the cause of intersex individuals across the continent. 2023

description.narrative: INDOTH4.2 African Commission Enhanced IHRD advocacy at the African Commission on Human and Peoples Rights (ACHPR) through participation IHRDs in NGO Forum, Resolution codrafting processes and Side Events

comment.narrative: BASOTH4.2 African Commission There is very nascent IHRD engagement at the ACHPR in the NGO Forum Resolution codrafting processes and Side Events
TAROTH4.2 African Commission Increased IHRD engagement at ACHPR involving up to 12 IHRDs in the NGO Forum Resolution codrafting processes and Side Events

CUROTH4.2. SIPD Uganda and The Centre for Human Rights convened a side event to launch a report on the human rights situation of intersex persons in Africa at the 73rd ordinary session of the African Commission on Human and Peoples rights in Banjul the Gambia. This event was held with the support of SIPD Ugandas partners The Intersex community of Zimbabwe ICoZ and the Intersex Persons Society of Kenya IPSK. 2022 SIPD played a pivotal role in facilitating activist participation at the 77th ordinary session of the ACHPR in Arusha. At this session Intersex Human Rights Defenders IHRDs engaged with commissioners participated in the NGO Forum and contributed to an intersex side event. This platform proved crucial in initiating discussions to enhance the Resolution and explore strategies for its implementation across African nations. Additionally SIPD received an invitation to meet with the EU delegation in Kampala where discussions focused on sharing best practices and showcasing activities from the BoM project. SIPD reaffirmed its commitment to supporting the intersex community especially in response to Ugandas enactment of the new AntiHomosexuality Act in 2023. Further strengthening their advocacy efforts SIPD Uganda and The Centre for Human Rights convened a side event during the 73rd ordinary session of the African Commission on Human and Peoples Rights in Banjul the Gambia. This event supported by SIPD Ugandas partners The Intersex community of Zimbabwe ICoZ and the Intersex Persons Society of Kenya IPSK served as the platform for launching a report on the human rights situation of intersex persons in Africa. Through collaborative initiatives like these organisations continue to raise awareness advocate for rights and advance the cause of intersex individuals across the continent. 2023

title.narrative: INDOTH4.4 International Advocacy/ CrossCutting Issues international advocacy integrates this actions crosscutting issues of a) gender equality; b) children and youth, c) HIV/AIDS; d) labour rights and core labour standards

description.narrative: INDOTH4.4 International Advocacy/ CrossCutting Issues international advocacy integrates this actions crosscutting issues of a) gender equality; b) children and youth, c) HIV/AIDS; d) labour rights and core labour standards

comment.narrative: BASOTH4.4 International Advocacy CrossCutting Issues Baseline to be set participatory with IHRDs THRDs and representatives of these crosscutting issues
TAROTH4.4 International Advocacy CrossCutting Issues Target to be set participatory with IHRDs THRDs and representatives of these crosscutting issues

CUROTH4.4. ILGA World conducted a dialogue with potential partners on the topic of HIV prevention. To begin activities in this area of work for Trans and Intersex communities ILGA World engaged with Love Alliance part of the Global Network of People Living with HIV. This dialogue is set to continue in 2023 with the potential of leading to a productive partnership. 2022 ILGA World continued its international advocacy efforts to safeguard the rights of intersex children and youth particularly focusing on protecting them from involuntary corrective surgeries genital mutilation and genderbased violence often encountered in educational environments. These endeavours also entail providing comprehensive support to parents of intersex children with a specific emphasis on assisting mothers. By addressing these pressing issues ILGA Worlds initiatives contribute to promoting gender equality and advancing the rights of genderdiverse intersex and transgender individuals alongside advocating for womens rights on a global scale. Through collaborative partnerships and advocacy campaigns ILGA World seeks to create inclusive and supportive environments that uphold the dignity and rights of all individuals regardless of their gender identity or expression. 2023

title.narrative: Other Outcome 5 (OTH5) Institutional Development enhanced Trans Fund autonomy and capacity and enhanced Intersex Fund institutionalisation and capacity

description.narrative: Other Outcome 5 (OTH5) Institutional Development enhanced Trans Fund autonomy and capacity and enhanced Intersex Fund institutionalisation and capacity

title.narrative: INDOTH5.1 Enhanced Trans Fund autonomy and capacity

description.narrative: INDOTH5.1 Enhanced Trans Fund autonomy and capacity

comment.narrative: BASOTH5.1 Trans Fund Autonomy The Trans Fund is not autonomous and does not have a strategic plan
TAROTH5.1 Trans Fund Autonomy The Trans Fund has developed organisational policies a strategy for incorporation and a 5year strategic plan based on the priorities of THRDs

CUROTH5.1 Trans Fund is autonomous as of 1 January 2022 and developed a strategic plan in 2021. 2022 ITFs staff portfolio grew from 5 in the previous reporting period to 7. 2022 The ITF also increased the number of donors by 25 by adding two new donors 2022 ITF embarked on a multifaceted Strategy for Incorporation spanning a threeyear timeline and entailing thorough research engagement of consultants and the transition towards becoming an independent entity. Significant milestones achieved in 2023 included the formalisation of the initial Board of Directors successful completion of the inaugural independent audit with favourable outcomes development of a chart of accounts and migration to a new grants management software system. Furthermore the ITF concluded its 5year strategic plan in 2021 with active involvement from leadership and the participation of over 30 stakeholders in the strategic planning process. 2023

title.narrative: INDOTH5.2 Enhanced Intersex Fund Institutionalisation and Capacity

description.narrative: INDOTH5.2 Enhanced Intersex Fund Institutionalisation and Capacity

comment.narrative: BASOTH5.2 Intersex Fund Institutionalisation and Capacity The Intersex Fund has only informal programmatic strategies only 1.5 staff and has not formally consulted with IHRDs about its structure and longterm direction since its inception

TAROTH5.2 Intersex Fund Institutionalisation and Capacity The Intersex Fund has more robust capacity including formal capacitybuilding grantmaking and advocacy strategies 2 fulltime staff and guidance from IHRDs about its structure and future direction.

CUROTH5.2 The Intersex Fund has 2 staff members. 2022 the IHRF had its first external evaluation through a participatory consultation process from March to April 2022 to evaluate the IHRFs contribution as well as assess perceptions of the state of the intersex movement and its evolving needs to ensure that the Fund aligns itself correspondingly with the needs and priorities of the Intersex movement and improves its institutional advantage in terms of financial and human Capacity. 2022

The value was achieved 2 TA provided by Intersex Fund to Intersex Asia including setting up governance structures and completing strategic planning 2020 Via one checkin call and numerous email engagements the Intersex Fund provided Intersex Asia with support identifying its capacitystrengthening priorities and provided advice on small grants that Intersex Asia was moving to IHRDs for pandemic support. 2021 Intersex Fund supported Intersex Asias capacity strengthening workshop which focused on addressing capacity gaps in organisational development financial management and project management among intersex groups from Taiwan Philippines Nepal India and Thailand. 2023

title.narrative: Specific Objective 2 (SO2): IHRDs, THRDs, and their allied social justice movements intensify their advocacy for intersex and trans rights at the local, national, regional, and global level

description.narrative: Specific Objective 2 (SO2): IHRDs, THRDs, and their allied social justice movements intensify their advocacy for intersex and trans rights at the local, national, regional, and global level

title.narrative: INDSO2.3. Regional level IHRDs and THRDs, and allied social justice movements in Africa, Asia and the Pacific intensify their advocacy for the rights and needs of intersex and trans people at the regional level

description.narrative: INDSO2.3. Regional level IHRDs and THRDs, and allied social justice movements in Africa, Asia and the Pacific intensify their advocacy for the rights and needs of intersex and trans people at the regional level

comment.narrative: ASSO2.3.1 Regional level African Commission limited awareness and visibility of an intersex human rights agenda at the African Commission on Human and Peoples Rights January 2020 BASSO2.3.2 Regional level Asia Pacific Forum of NHRIs limited awareness and visibility of trans human rights among NHRIs in Asia and the Pacific January 2020 BASSO2.3.3 Regional level Regional Alliances Width depth diversity of regional alliances varies across regions and are attuned to regional IHRD or THRD context.

TARSO2.3.1 Regional level African Commission increased awareness and visibility of the intersex human rights agenda at the African Commission on Human and Peoples Rights 2023TARSO2.3.2 Regional level Asia Pacific Forum of NHRIs increased awareness and visibility of trans human rights among NHRIs in Asia and the Pacific 2023TARSO2.3.3 Regional level Regional Alliances Targets vary across regions and are attuned to regional IHRD or THRD context.

CURSO2.3.1 Regional level African Commission limited awareness visibility continues as as significant advocacy has not been possible due to pandemic 2021CURSO2.3.2 Regional level Asia Pacific Forum of NHRIs limited awareness visibility continues as as significant advocacy has not been possible due to pandemic 2021CURSO2.3.3 Regional level Regional Alliances Africa Intersex The African Intersex Movement AIM moved to formalize and strengthen their network including by creating a strategic plan and establishing a secretariat. AIM has also made new connections with IHRDs in East and West Africa. Africa Trans the Africa Trans Network ATN which was established in February 2020 as a network of trans organisations and three regional THRD networks in Africa the East Africa Trans Health Advocacy Network the West African Trans Forum WATF and Transat recorded exponential growth in 2021. Asia Intersex Intersex Asia was able engage IHRDs from countries that the intersex movement had not previously reached including Mongolia Singapore and Pakistan. 2021 APTN sought to amplify the regional collaboration of THRDs between countries towards transformative intersectional grassrootled movement building. The two convenings were important to share advocacy and programmatic tools build a space for subregional coalition building and also gather current data and information in a quickly shifting climate. The South East Asia Convening was held in Bangkok in September 2022. The South Asia Convening was held in Kathmandu in January 2023. 2022 Intersex Asia was also invited to attend the EUTaiwan LGBTI Human Rights Conference in October 2022 to share more about the experiences of IHRDs in Asia. This was the first intersexspecific panel hosted by a governmental human rights conference in Taiwan. 2022 The AIM Steering Committee kickstarted the process of formal registration and hire of a coordinator. Pan Africa ILGA PAI has engaged AIM extensively in the past several months to contribute to the continentwide mapping of crossmovement building and advocacy opportunities and has invited AIM to hold a selforganized Intersex preconference at PAIs 6th regional conference to be held in Mauritius in July 2023. 2022

comment.narrative: BASSO2.1.1 Local level Intersex no or very little awareness and visibility of intersex human rights in most local contexts. BASSO2.1.2 Local level Trans limited awareness and visibility of trans human rights in most local contexts.

TARSO2.1.1 Local level Intersex Increased awareness and visibility of intersex human rights in local contexts 2023 TARSO2.1.2 Local level Trans Increased awareness and visibility of trans human rights in local contexts 2023

CURSO2.1.1 Local level Intersex Grantee partners focused on rights awareness for IHRDs and their families 2021 There has been an increasing number of new intersexled groups including in countries like Japan and India. In Africa new intersexled groups in Tanzania Cameroon Tunisia and Ghana were established. 2022. CURSO2.1.2 Local level Trans Grantee partners focused on rights awareness for THRDs 2021

title.narrative: INDSO2.2. National level IHRDs and THRDs, and allied social justice movements in countries, in which BoM operates, intensify their advocacy for the rights and needs of intersex and trans people at the national level

description.narrative: INDSO2.2. National level IHRDs and THRDs, and allied social justice movements in countries, in which BoM operates, intensify their advocacy for the rights and needs of intersex and trans people at the national level

comment.narrative: BASSO2.2.1 National level Intersex no or very little awareness and visibility of intersex human rights in most national contexts and policy conversations. BASSO2.2.2 National level Trans limited awareness and visibility of trans human rights in most national contexts and policy conversations.

TARSO2.2.1 National level Intersex Increased awareness and visibility of intersex human rights in national policy conversations 2023 TARSO2.2.2 National level Trans Increased awareness and visibility of trans human rights in national policy conversations 2023

National level Intersex National Reports in progress in Kenya Uganda and Zimbabwe Kenya Intersex Taskforce established 2021 ISSA contributed to a historic national policy dialogue on intersex and trans rights in South Africa held in partnership with the European Union in Nov 2021. IPSK contributed to appointment of first openly intersex govt commissioner in Kenya. 2021 IHRDled organizations have been engaged in advocacy for the rights of intersex persons and strengthened their relationships with policymakers to increase their influence in policy discussions. IHRDs use research and advocacy tools to continue highlighting legal and social gaps including Nepal Kenya Zimbabwe Botswana Ghana and Uganda. 2022National level Trans Resilient held two consultative meetings with lawyers in Bangladesh around name and gender marker issues on legal documents. In Malaysia SEED held meetings with members of the judiciary and legislature including members of Parliament regarding legal reform and access to justice. 2021

Historic crossregional statement by 53 UN member states calling for concrete measures to combat harmful practices violence and discrimination against intersex persons. title.narrative: INDSO2.5. CrossCutting Issues IHRDs and THRDs, and allied social justice movements advocate more intersectionally and inclusive of the crosscutting issues of a) gender equality; b) children and youth; c) HIV/AIDS and d) labour rights and core labour standards

description.narrative: INDSO2.5. CrossCutting Issues IHRDs and THRDs, and allied social justice movements advocate more intersectionally and inclusive of the crosscutting issues of a) gender equality; b) children and youth; c) HIV/AIDS and d) labour rights and core labour standards

comment.narrative: BASSO2.5 CrossCutting Issues Presence of intersectionality and identified crosscutting issues in advocacy and advocacy priorities with some intentionality
TARSO2.5 CrossCutting Issues Greater and more intentional presence of intersectionality and identified crosscutting issues in advocacy and advocacy priorities 2023

CURSO2.5 CrossCutting Issues ILGA led a major targeted effort to conduct global crosscutting advocacy illustrating the critical overlaps between the rights of women and of trans persons through the lens of gender equality via a side event Feminist and LGBTQI Movements Uniting is Our Strength in collaboration with the Permanent Missions of the Republic of Argentina and the Kingdom of the Netherlands and numerous civil society organisations across the gender equality LGBTI and womens rights spectrum. Additionally ILGA World actively engaged and influenced the resolutions on Menstrual Hygiene and Gender Equality on Violence Against Women on HIV and Human Rights on Internet and Enjoyment of Human Rights Civil Society Space among others. ILGA World successfully fought against the issue of sexsegregated toilets which was raised in the Menstrual Hygiene resolution. 2021
